title: webhook-runner hook configuration
description: Configuration for a webhook-runner hook. Place this file as hook.json inside a named directory under the hooks root, next to the mandatory Dockerfile that bakes the hook's code into its image.

descriptions.$schema: URI of the JSON Schema this hook.json is validated against. Set it to https://sites.pazer.build/webhook-runner/branch/master/hook.schema.json (the legacy https://wow-look-at-my.github.io/webhook-runner/hook.schema.json is still accepted, but serves frozen 2026-07-15 content).
descriptions.api_key: API key for bearer-token authentication. Checked against the X-API-Key header (or api_key_header). May reference a secret as ${NAME}, resolved from the hook's sops-encrypted secrets.sops.env first, then the runner host's environment; if the reference is unresolvable the hook fails closed (all requests rejected). Recommended for most hooks.
descriptions.api_key_header: HTTP header to read the API key from. Default: X-API-Key.
descriptions.command: Optional override of the image's CMD, passed to docker run after the image name. Every hook runs the image webhook-runner builds from the Dockerfile in its directory (tagged by content hash) — code is baked in and immutable per run; when command is omitted, the image's CMD/ENTRYPOINT runs.
descriptions.concurrency_group: Name of a concurrency group declared in concurrency.json at the hooks root. At most that group's limit of runs (counted across every hook sharing the group) execute at once; the rest queue as 'pending' with their timeout not yet counting. Referencing a group not declared in concurrency.json is a load/validation error. Omit for unbounded concurrency.
descriptions.description: Human-readable description of what this hook does.
descriptions.dind: When true, give the container an anonymous volume at /var/lib/docker so it can host its OWN nested container daemon: an inner daemon cannot run its overlay storage driver on top of the outer container's overlay, so that path must be a volume rather than the layered rootfs. --rm auto-removes it when the run ends, so inner storage never leaks between runs, and the host's own docker daemon is NEVER exposed (no socket is mounted). A hook listing /var/lib/docker in `scratch` supplies that mount itself and no volume is added (two mounts on one destination is a docker error). NO PRIVILEGE IS ADDED: --privileged is refused by ruling, because it is host-root-equivalent -- it hands a uid-0 container an unmasked /proc, and a writable /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern alone runs a helper as real root on the HOST. These containers execute other people's CI, so the nested daemon has to be a ROOTLESS one (dockerd-rootless.sh, needing a user namespace, fuse-overlayfs or vfs storage, and no iptables). A root `dockerd` will not start and the run fails saying so, rather than degrading quietly. Applied identically on the live-run and `webhook-runner test` paths, so an image is proved in CI rather than on a runner.
descriptions.enable: The hook's DEFAULT enabled state. When false, the hook loads disabled: deliveries are rejected (503) and scheduled runs are skipped exactly as if the operator kill switch were off, until an operator explicitly enables it. The dashboard/admin runtime override (POST /hooks/{id}/enable|disable, persisted server-side) always takes precedence over this default, in both directions. Absent = enabled, so existing hooks are unchanged.
descriptions.github_status: GitHub commit status updates for this hook's runs: when a delivery's payload carries a repo + head SHA, the runner posts 'pending' as the run starts and 'success'/'error' when it finishes. A run with no commit to point at posts nothing.
descriptions.networks: Docker networks to attach the container to.
descriptions.public_key: Base64 or hex-encoded Ed25519 public key. When set, incoming requests must include a valid Ed25519 signature of the body in the signature header.
descriptions.run_title: Template for the friendly display title of this hook's runs, shown by the dashboard in place of the opaque run id (e.g. "{{repository.full_name}}#{{pull_request.number}}" renders "wow-look-at-my/go-toolchain#47"). A {{...}} placeholder names a dotted path into the parsed JSON payload ("pull_request.number", array elements by numeric index) or a request header via the "header:" prefix — exactly skip_if's key syntax and bounded traversal. Resolution is graceful and never blocks a run: each placeholder becomes the scalar leaf's string form (numbers as their JSON literal, true/false as those words); a missing path, an object/array, and JSON null become empty; when EVERY placeholder resolves empty the run simply gets no title (consumers fall back to the run id), otherwise pure-separator literals stranded next to empty placeholders are dropped and whitespace collapses. A template with no placeholders is a static title, always set. Resolved once at run creation, before skip_if — skipped runs are titled too; schedule-triggered runs resolve against the synthetic schedule payload and fall back to "schedule". Titles are capped at 200 characters, and a state hook can rename its run mid-flight via POST /title on the state API. A malformed template (unterminated "{{", empty "{{}}") is a load/validation error.
descriptions.seccomp: Narrow the container's syscall filter. Absent means the default: docker's builtin seccomp profile, unmodified. The block names specific relaxations -- there is deliberately no way to point at an arbitrary profile or to say 'unconfined'. seccomp.userns (default false): let the container build an in-container sandbox (bubblewrap, and so `dats` on its default backend). TWO obstructions come off together, because either alone leaves bwrap dead. Syscalls: docker's default profile plus an ungated allow for unshare/clone/clone3/setns and mount/umount2/pivot_root, which the default permits only for a container holding CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Paths: docker's masked and read-only /proc paths (systempaths=unconfined), because the kernel refuses a fresh procfs inside a user namespace while the visible /proc carries them. THIS REQUIRES A DAEMON THAT REMAPS CONTAINER ROOT (userns-remap) and the run FAILS on one that does not, naming it. That is the interlock: on a container whose root is the host's root, an unmasked /proc means a writable /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern, whose helper the HOST kernel runs as real root -- dropping CAP_SYS_ADMIN does not refuse that write. Under remap the file is owned by a uid outside the container's map, so the write is refused on the DAC check while bwrap still mounts its /proc. An AUDITED opt-in like dind: unprivileged user namespaces have a real CVE history, so enable it only for trusted, operator-curated hooks. Applied identically on the live-run and `webhook-runner test` paths.
descriptions.script: Run a script file from the hook directory: derives the container command as <interpreter> <file> [args...]. Like all hook code, the script is baked into the hook's image by its Dockerfile (never mounted), so the interpreter must be installed in that image. An explicit command overrides the derived one.
descriptions.secret: Legacy: shared secret for HMAC-SHA256 signature verification. Prefer api_key or public_key.
descriptions.settings: The hook's OWN configuration: any JSON object shape it wants. webhook-runner never interprets it -- it validates the object against the settings.schema.json shipped next to this manifest (declaring settings without that file is a load error) and hands it to the container as a read-only file at $HOOK_SETTINGS_FILE. This replaced the `env` block, which mixed hook-private config into the runner's own parsed keys, forced every value to be a string, and was validated by nobody. Settings are read per RUN, so changing them takes effect on the next run without rebuilding the image. REFERENCES: a string value may contain ${settings:a.b[2].c} (another value in this same document) or ${env:NAME} (a variable from the entity's secrets.sops.env, then the runner host's environment). ${settings:...} resolves at LOAD, so the schema validates the RESOLVED value and a bad path is a load error; a whole-string reference keeps the referenced value's type. ${env:NAME} resolves when the container starts -- an unresolvable one FAILS THE RUN rather than becoming an empty string -- so at load the schema sees the reference text, and a field meant to hold one must permit it (e.g. anyOf with a ^\\$\\{env: pattern). Credentials belong here only under the same private-repo posture as the rest of the manifest; the admin API exposes the top-level KEY NAMES only.
descriptions.signature_header: HTTP header containing the signature. Default: X-Signature-Ed25519 for public_key auth, X-Hub-Signature-256 for legacy HMAC.
descriptions.skip_if: Declarative skip conditions. An authenticated delivery matching any condition (entries are ORed) is SKIPPED: answered immediately, recorded as a first-class run with status 'skipped' naming the matched condition, and given NO container (no image build, no concurrency slot, no docker run). Keys within one condition are ANDed. A key is a dotted path into the parsed JSON payload ("action", "workflow_run.conclusion", array elements by numeric index) or a request header via the "header:" prefix ("header:x-github-event", name case-insensitive). Comparisons are over stringified scalar leaves (numbers as their JSON literal, true/false/null as those words); objects/arrays are not leaves, and a missing path does not match — evaluation is total and fails toward running the hook. Evaluated only AFTER authentication. Malformed conditions (unknown operator, non-compiling regex, empty condition) are a load/validation error.
descriptions.synchronous: When true, the server holds the HTTP response open until the container exits. Default: false (returns 202 immediately).
descriptions.tests: Test commands for the hook's scripts. Each entry is an argv array that `webhook-runner test` runs in the hook's built image, so tests exercise exactly the baked code (copy test files into the image and set WORKDIR so relative paths resolve). Tests run without the hook's env, secrets, or payload and must be self-contained; they never run when the hook is triggered.
descriptions.timeout: Go duration for the container timeout (e.g. "5m", "30s"): the absolute processing ceiling, counted from container launch regardless of output. Omit for no absolute ceiling; pair with idle_timeout so a hung run still dies (a hook that omits both runs until it exits).
descriptions.user: User/UID to run the container as (--user flag).
descriptions.workdir: Working directory inside the container (--workdir flag).

schedule.description: Go duration (e.g. "5m", "1h") to fire this hook on a fixed interval, in addition to any HTTP trigger. A scheduled run goes through the same pipeline as an HTTP-triggered one (tracked, gated by concurrency_group, KV-enabled, shown on the dashboard) with a synthetic payload marking it schedule-triggered. On startup, and whenever the schedule is newly added or its interval changes, the hook fires immediately, then every interval; the scheduler skips a tick while a previous run of the same hook is still in flight (skip-if-already-running). Omit for HTTP-triggered only.

scratch.description: Absolute CONTAINER paths whose writes must land on the operator's scratch filesystem (WEBHOOK_RUNNER_SCRATCH_DIR) instead of under docker's data-root. Each path is bind-mounted from a directory private to this run, created before the container starts and removed when it ends; a serve boot also sweeps subtrees left by a process that died mid-run. Declare the paths that carry real volume -- a CI job's checkout tree, a nested daemon's image store at /var/lib/docker -- and pair them with tmpfs for the rest. This is a REQUIREMENT, not a hint: a run whose hook declares scratch paths on a server with no scratch directory configured FAILS, rather than quietly writing to the disk the declaration exists to spare. A dind hook listing /var/lib/docker gets its inner daemon's store from scratch and no anonymous volume is added (two mounts on one destination is a docker error). Paths must be absolute and clean, may not be "/", and may not repeat within scratch or across tmpfs.

tmpfs.description: Absolute CONTAINER paths backed by RAM (--tmpfs) instead of disk: writes never touch a disk at all, so they cost no device wear and vanish with the container. The companion to scratch: scratch takes what must survive on a disk or is too big for memory, tmpfs takes the rest, and between them a hook can account for every path it writes to -- which is what read_only_rootfs then enforces. An entry may carry docker's option suffix ("/tmp:size=4g"), passed through untouched. SIZE ANYTHING THAT COULD GROW: an unbounded tmpfs may reach half of host RAM, and several of them on one container, multiplied by the concurrency limit, can exhaust the host. Same path rules as scratch, and a path may not appear in both.

read_only_rootfs.description: Run the container with --read-only, so the ONLY writable locations are its scratch and tmpfs mounts. Without this, "the heavy paths are on scratch" is a claim about the paths somebody remembered to list: any other write still lands in the container's writable layer under docker's data-root, silently, which is exactly the disk the declarations exist to spare. With it, an unlisted write fails loudly instead. Opt-in because it can only be proven per image -- a program that writes somewhere unlisted breaks under it -- so prove it in the hook's own tests, which `webhook-runner test` runs with these same flags (scratch paths backed by tmpfs there, since a CI runner has no scratch filesystem). Default: false.
read_only_rootfs.$comment: Enforcement, not decoration: without it the other two fields cannot be trusted, because an undeclared path fails silently onto the data-root.

state.description: When true, opt the hook into the persistent KV store. The runner injects HOOK_KV_URL (http://localhost:9002) and HOOK_KV_TOKEN (a per-hook bearer token whose namespace is this hook's ID), and a proxy shim entrypoint, so the hook reaches the state API at a plain localhost URL with any HTTP client (no networking, no published port). The hook's data persists across its runs and across server restarts, isolated from other hooks. Default: false (no KV access).

idle_timeout.description: Go duration (e.g. "5m"): kill the run once the container has produced no output (stdout or stderr) for this long. Any output byte resets the idle clock. Arms at container launch -- after the concurrency-group slot is acquired -- so a queued run never idles out. Independent of timeout (the absolute ceiling); both may be set, and whichever fires first ends the run with status "timeout" (an idle kill carries a distinguishable "idle timeout ... (no output)" error message). Omit for no idle limit.
